headline: Atlassian launches AI suite for Jira to boost developer productivity
summary: The new suite aims to streamline developer workflows, with internal studies reporting a 44% increase in task completion efficiency and a 36% reduction in PR cycle time.
details: Atlassian has launched a new AI suite for Jira, designed to streamline the developer workflow from ticket to pull request. This aims to collapse the traditional handoff process, where specs were re-keyed, into a single, automated loop.

The suite introduces "Coding-agent handoff," allowing Jira work items to be assigned directly to AI agents like Claude Code, Cursor, or GitHub Copilot. A built-in Jira Coding Agent also converts work items into pull requests without needing a local clone, simplifying routine tasks.

Jira Planner is a key component, leveraging historical data from Jira and Confluence to draft technical specifications directly into Confluence. This feature can assemble comprehensive specs in minutes that would take a human PM a week to gather.

Another feature is Slack filing via @Jira, enabling users to tag @Jira in a Slack thread to automatically create a work item with the conversation context. This eliminates the common issue of tasks being forgotten or delayed.

Atlassian's head of engineering for DevAI, Ming Wu, stated the goal is to keep developers in their editors by bringing Jira to them. The suite addresses the "recompute" cost of switching contexts, ensuring the plan remains consistent from end to end.

This initiative represents a significant piece of developer-experience engineering, moving beyond decorative AI features to remove actual workflow friction. The Planner → spec → agent loop is designed to maintain the plan's shape throughout the development process.

Internal Atlassian studies report a 44% increase in agent task completion efficiency and a 36% reduction in pull request cycle time. While these figures are vendor claims and not independently verified, they align with the expected benefits of the streamlined loop.

Users are advised to monitor PR quality over mere count, as a fast agent producing sloppy PRs can create a faster backlog. Ensuring agents target the correct components and files is also crucial to avoid "fast loop, wrong target" failures.

Future plans include integration with OpenAI's Codex, which will expand the choice of coding agents available within Jira. This architecture also opens the door for further automation, such as agents that can select their own reviewers.

headline_marked: [[Skullcandy Crusher 1080 ANC headphones launch]] with Bose QuietControl and TrueSpatial audio
headline: Skullcandy Crusher 1080 ANC headphones launch with Bose QuietControl and TrueSpatial audio
summary: Available today for $279.99, the new Crusher 1080 ANC integrate Bose's industry-leading noise cancellation and head-tracking spatial audio, enhancing clarity and reducing distortion.
details: Skullcandy has launched a new version of its Crusher wireless headphones, the Crusher 1080 ANC, available today for $279.99. These headphones integrate several Bose audio technologies, including QuietControl ANC and head-tracking spatial audio, in black, candy, primer, and cement color options.

The Crusher line is known for its dedicated bass drivers, but Skullcandy admits this can lead to audio quality loss with heavy bass boost. The new 1080 ANC model addresses this with redesigned drivers featuring a stiffer diaphragm material, aiming for enhanced clarity and reduced distortion at higher volumes.

The Crusher 1080 ANC are the first non-Bose headphones to feature Bose’s TrueSpatial audio with head tracking, working whether stationary or on the move. They also include Bose’s WaveForm audio engine for balanced sound and industry-leading QuietControl ANC with six microphones, adapting to ambient noise levels.

Bose’s SpeechClarity technology is also integrated, reducing noise for clear voice calls. Battery life is estimated at up to 60 hours without ANC or 50 hours with it on, with a 10-minute rapid charge providing four hours of playback. Additional features include multipoint pairing, auto reconnect, wear detection, Bluetooth 5.3 with LE Audio, and Auracast support.
